2023 to 2024 · Society

A spotlight, an accelerator and an Earthshot that got away

In 2023 the project was accepted into the Third Derivative climate accelerator, won the Climate Spotlight Award at the Ocean Impact Pitchfest, and was nominated for the Earthshot Prize. Here is what each of those was, and was not.

Recognition is useful to a small research project mostly as a signal to others that the idea has been looked at seriously. We keep these on the website for that reason, with their proper labels.

Third Derivative, 2023

In the summer of 2023 the project was accepted into Third Derivative, the climate technology accelerator founded by RMI and New Energy Nexus, as part of Cohort 23-2. Accelerator participation came with mentorship, a network of corporate partners and an early investment. It is a programme, not an award, and it was awarded to the commercial company, Kelp Island, rather than to the Society.

Ocean Impact Pitchfest, 2023

At the Ocean Impact Organisation's Pitchfest in Sydney in late 2023, Kelp Island was named Climate Spotlight winner, an award presented by the offshore wind developer Star of the South. The project was not the overall Pitchfest winner. The award recognised the climate case: kelp farming paired with a durable building material that keeps biogenic carbon out of the atmosphere for the life of the structure.

The Earthshot nomination

In November 2023 Ashoka nominated the project for the 2024 cycle of the Earthshot Prize, in the "Fix our Climate" category. The nomination was built around a bold claim: that kelp farming and SeaBrick carbon storage, scaled over decades, could sequester a very large share of global emissions. The project was not selected. The feedback, in short, was "too early": the winning projects were much further along. We think that was fair, and it changed how we talk about the work. The claims on this site are deliberately smaller than the ones in that submission.

Research funding

Alongside those, the project received a BC government-supported feasibility study through the Construction Foundation of BC in 2023, and in late 2024 a $25,000 Ocean Startup grant from Canada's Ocean Supercluster to validate a new waterproofing approach (see Keeping the water out).
